articles.title: Quenton Nelson to Have Surgery on Knee Injury, Latest News on Seahawks Star's Status After Trade
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks will have to wait at least another week to see newly-acquired guard Quenton Nelson play his second game for the franchise.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks will have to wait at least another week to see newly-acquired guard Quenton Nelson play his second game for the franchise.

Nelson will be out Sunday against the visiting Arizona Cardinals after undergoing a "minor procedure" on his knee, head coach Mike Macdonald announced.

He is considered week-to-week but won't be placed on IR, according to Macdonald.

The news comes 10 days after the Seahawks gave up a 2027 third-round pick and 2028 fifth-rounder in order to acquire Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts.

Nelson was on the field for every Seahawks offensive snap while playing at left guard opposite Grey Zabel during the team's Monday loss to the visiting Chicago Bears.

Macdonald said Nelson had passed a physical after arriving in Seattle, but during Monday's game aggravated an issue stemming from his final contest with the Colts back on Oct. 25.

"In short, he had something he was dealing with when he got here," Macdonald said. "We re-imaged it, and it was aggravated to some degree. So we've done the due diligence, and everybody agrees that it's best to take care of it now and play the long game."

Macdonald said the team had discussed keeping Zabel at right guard after moving him there in the wake of Nelson's injury, but ultimately decided to slide Zabel to left while former starting right guard Anthony Bradford will return to his previous position.

The Seahawks are scheduled for a Week 11 bye. The decision not to place Nelson on IR indicates the team expects him back by at least the game after, when Seattle plays a road game against the San Francisco 49ers on Nov. 19.

Macdonald confirmed Friday Drew Lock, who has been dealing with an elbow injury, is on track to start in place of injured starter Sam Darnold.

Darnold and Nelson won't be the only injury absences for the Seahawks this weekend. Defensive tackle Leonard Williams, wide receiver Rashid Shaheed and linebacker Uchenna Nwosu will also be out for Saturday's game, according to Macdonald.

The Seahawks will look to adjust to those gaps in the lineup before kicking off Week 9 action Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: A.J. Brown, Christian McCaffrey, NFL Injury Statuses and Fantasy Impact for Week 9
articles.summary: The New England Patriots will once again be without A.J. Brown.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots will once again be without A.J. Brown.

Brown was ruled out of Week 9's clash with the Green Bay Packers due to his knee injury.

The news is more promising with Christian McCaffrey, who practiced on Friday afternoon.

McCaffrey's status hasn't been confirmed yet, but things appear to be trending in the right direction for the San Francisco 49ers running back.

Below is a look at all of the significant injury news affecting fantasy football matchups in Week 9.

New England's prized offseason acquisition will once again be out on Sunday.

A.J. Brown's knee injury kept him out of practice all week and will make him miss the clash with the Green Bay Packers.

The good news for the Patriots is that they've been used to Brown's injury situation. He has 101 yards on nine catches in three appearances in 2026.

Demario Douglas and Hunter Henry have been popular waiver-wire pickups throughout the regular season because of their increased roles in the passing game.

Efton Chism, who had five receptions last week, and big-play threat Kyle Williams are the other pass-catching options, but they don't carry much fantasy football value with them.

Rhamondre Stevenson could be in for an uptick in catches on Sunday. He's caught all eight of his targets in the last two weeks.

The New York Giants have the best matchup on paper for wide receivers among the teams playing on Sunday. Darnell Mooney or Malachi Fields are intriguing sleeper options off the waiver wire to replace Brown because of the matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles.

Cooper Kupp fits into the deep sleeper category as well because the Seattle Seahawks face an Arizona Cardinals defense that is tied with the Buffalo Bills for the most touchdowns conceded to wide receivers.

Dallas' Ryan Flournoy and Adonai Mitchell of the New York Jets are worth looks because of their increased roles in their respective offenses.

Christian McCaffrey was present at Friday's 49ers practice.

That's a positive sign for the running back, who missed practice on Wednesday and was limited on Thursday due to a hamstring issue.

McCaffrey and the 49ers have an ideal matchup on their hands in Week 9 against a Raiders defense that allowed 30 points or more in each of the last five games.

McCaffrey is already among the top scorers each week, but he could take the throne of top point scorer in fantasy football if he plays and dominates the Las Vegas defense.

Kaelon Black is worth rostering just in case McCaffrey isn't 100 percent, or the game turns into a blowout.

The rookie running back from Indiana had 63 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in the 49ers' loss to the Atlanta Falcons two weeks ago.

articles.title: 49ers' Kyle Shanahan Drops Brutally Honest Quote on Brandon Aiyuk in Video Ahead of WR's Return
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan doesn't care that wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is meeting with the team at its business offices on Friday.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan doesn't care that wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is meeting with the team at its business offices on Friday.

"No clue, your guess is as good as mine," Shanahan said during his Friday press conference when a reporter asked him what was going to happen.

The reporter then asked Shanahan what he would like to see happen, and the coach replied: "Could care less."

Aiyuk Addresses Future at 49ers Facility

Aiyuk's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, told ESPN's Adam Schefter that the team planned to meet with the 49ers at 3 p.m. PT on Friday.

The 49ers placed Aiyuk on the team's reserve/left squad list in Dec. 2025 .

In Oct. 2024 , the former Arizona State star suffered a torn ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee during a game against the Kansas City Chiefs, ending his season.

Aiyuk didn't play next year either, and any chance that he would return ended with with the placement on the reserve/left squad list.

Shanahan told reporters why following the 49ers' 37-24 win over the Tennessee Titans.

"We haven't seen him in forever," Shanahan said. "That's the decision they make. It's been pretty simple for me. I haven't seen him in a month. It hasn't been an issue with our team at all. We've been plugging away. No big deal. It's something we've been used to for a while."

Aiyuk's time with the 49ers is up. Shanahan has clearly "moved on," as he indicated earlier this week.

However, he's still under contract with the team after signing a four-year, $120 million contract extension with San Francisco in 2024.

Rosenhaus has turned in paperwork to have Aiyuk reinstated.

But he won't be back with San Francisco, so the question is how the 49ers and Aiyuk can best part ways.

As far as the 49ers' side, general manager John Lynch said the situation was "fluid" on KNBR's Murph & Markus show (h/t Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle ).

"I'm gonna kind of leave it at that, because I've been recommended to do so, and I think it's the right thing to do," Lynch said.

"We'll look for a pathway for both sides here that works. ... I think everything's possible. I will say this: We've worked with (agent Drew Rosenhaus) a lot. Drew is a good guy to deal with. He's reasonable, he's got integrity. … We'll see how this thing goes. I think I'll just leave it at that."

There also has been (and presumably will be) a lot of money involved here.

In the summer of 2025, the 49ers voided $27 million in guaranteed money for 2026 on Aiyuk's contract because he missed rehab sessions, per ESPN's Nick Wagoner .

However, per Josh Dubow of the Associated Press, the NFL told Aiyuk he owes the team $13 million he has previously received in bonus money:

"A person with knowledge of the situation said the league sent Aiyuk and the NFL Players Association a letter Thursday saying that he owes the 49ers the money based on bonuses he was paid after signing a four-year, $120 million extension just before the start of the 2024 season. The person spoke on condition of anonymity because the letter was not released."

Ultimately, Aiyuk's time with San Francisco finally appears to be nearing its end, culminating a long and drawn-out years-long saga.

articles.title: NFL Tells Brandon Aiyuk He Owes the 49ers About $13 Million, AP Source Says
articles.summary: SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) — The NFL has told disgruntled receiver Brandon Aiyuk that he needs to repay the San Francisco 49ers about $13 million he previously received in bonuses as he tries to get reinstated to the team's roster.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) — The NFL has told disgruntled receiver Brandon Aiyuk that he needs to repay the San Francisco 49ers about $13 million he previously received in bonuses as he tries to get reinstated to the team's roster.

Aiyuk has submitted his paperwork to the NFL to get back, and he arrived alongside new agent Drew Rosenhaus for a meeting Friday afternoon at the team's business offices, which are near the team facility at Levi's Stadium.

"Brandon is here to meet with the team. Fortunately he's feeling good physically. He's healthy, he's ready to get back to work," Rosenhaus said. "I don't really have any comment about where he's going to play. We'll keep that between us and the Niners but obviously we're here with all the right intentions."

Aiyuk Addresses Future at 49ers Facility

A person with knowledge of the situation said the league sent Aiyuk and the NFL Players Association a letter Thursday saying that he owes the 49ers the money based on bonuses he was paid after signing a four-year, $120 million extension just before the start of the 2024 season. The person spoke on condition of anonymity because the letter was not released.

Aiyuk did not address the financial issues as he arrived for the meeting.

"I'm feeling great, feeling healthy. Long recovery process, long rehab process," Aiyuk said. "But I'm back to 100 percent and looking to get reinstated into the National Football League."

The meeting lasted about an hour, and Rosenhaus declined to share details. "To be continued," he said.

Coach Kyle Shanahan said he would have no role in the meeting and didn't care at all what happens, saying that he has moved on from Aiyuk and the situation isn't a distraction at all.

"It's been over for our football team for a long time," Shanahan said. "I don't hear much except questions about it today. But it's not too big of a deal for me to answer."

The Ringer first reported that the Niners were seeking the money back from Aiyuk.

San Francisco general manager John Lynch told the team's flagship radio station KNBR on Thursday that it was a "unique" situation that the team was trying to work through.

"My job is to look out for the best interests of the 49ers, and as such, in this particular situation, we're working with the NFL management council to navigate through kind of a different situation," Lynch said. "It's fluid. I'm going to kind of leave it at that because I've been recommended to do so, and I think it's the right thing to do. We'll look for a pathway for both sides here that works."

Aiyuk hasn't played a game in more than two years since going down with a knee injury in October 2024 and has been on the reserve/left squad list after leaving the Niners late last season.

He fired agent Ryan Williams during his long-running dispute with the 49ers and was without representation until he recently hired Rosenhaus.

Aiyuk will remain under contract with the 49ers after he is reinstated by the NFL. Lynch previously has said he doesn't expect Aiyuk to play for the Niners again.

The 49ers previously voided $27 million guaranteed in Aiyuk's contract for 2026 for failing to participate in meetings and other team activities last summer when he was rehabilitating his knee injury.

Aiyuk signed the big extension just before the start of the 2024 season following a lengthy contract hold-in that kept him out of training camp. He was coming off a 2023 season when he had 75 catches for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns and was a second-team All-Pro.

Aiyuk had only 25 catches for 374 yards in seven games in 2024 before getting injured. The 28-year-old has 294 catches for 4,305 yards and 25 TDs since being drafted in the first round in 2020.

AP Pro Football Writer Rob Maaddi contributed to this report.

articles.title: "He’s just, he’s soft": Travis Kelce’s GOAT tight end case faces fresh scrutiny as Patriots champion explains why Rob Gronkowski ranks above him
articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s standing among the NFL’s greatest tight ends has come under fresh scrutiny after former New England Patriots player Christian Fauria
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s standing among the NFL’s greatest tight ends has come under fresh scrutiny after former New England Patriots player Christian Fauria questioned one important part of his game. Fauria, a two-time Super Bowl champion, believes Rob Gronkowski deserves the top spot, with Tony Gonzalez second. His criticism of Kelce focused on blocking, an area where he feels the Kansas City Chiefs star does not show enough willingness. However, Fauria also admitted that the skill may not be as important to the position as some believe.Christian Fauria questions Travis Kelce’s blocking abilitySpeaking on the NESN podcast, Fauria explained why Gonzalez earned his second-place ranking. He felt the former Chiefs and Atlanta Falcons tight end deserved more recognition for his work as a blocker, particularly given his production as a receiver.“Tony Gonzalez never gets enough credit for being a capable blocker,” Fauria said. “Now, he didn’t destroy people, but he was pretty damn good for a guy that caught as many passes as he did. So, I think Tony’s my number two.”Kelce received a less favourable assessment. Fauria did not question his receiving skills, but he had reservations about his approach to blocking.“Now, Kelce gets a lot of flak because … he’s soft. He’s just, he’s soft, right? That’s no disrespect,” Fauria said. He then clarified his criticism: “Doesn’t mean he couldn’t beat you up in a fight, but when it comes to blocking, I just don’t think he has a willingness to do it. But I also don’t know if it matters as much.”Interestingly, Fauria's argument also included a reference to former San Francisco 49ers coach Bill Walsh. He recalled Walsh's scouting criteria for tight ends, which stressed the importance of being willing to block rather than necessarily excelling at it.“He said you needed to be a willing blocker. And that’s what Travis Kelce is. That’s what Shannon Sharpe is. They’re willing blockers. It doesn’t mean they’re great at it. They’re not moving or setting the edge, but they’re not blowing up running plays,” Fauria said.Rob Gronkowski’s versatility separates him from Travis KelceFauria had little hesitation when explaining why Gronkowski topped his list. The former Patriots star could contribute in almost every aspect of the tight end position, making him a more complete player in Fauria's assessment.“Gronk could do everything all those other guys can do,” Fauria said. “He could find the void. He could finesse you in zone. He could run deep. He can run seams. He can run shallows. He can run crossers.”He also highlighted Gronkowski's ability to operate from the slot, much like Gonzalez, Shannon Sharpe and Kelce. Fauria ultimately said that if the position were judged by its complete responsibilities, “I don’t know how you could say it’s anyone other than Gronk.”Kelce's numbers, meanwhile, show why he remains a major part of this discussion. Through eight weeks of the 2026 season, he had recorded 29 catches for 410 yards and two touchdowns. His 3.9-yard average separation at the catch point also ranked among the league's best, according to Next Gen Stats. He held an 85.9 grade in PFN's NFL TE Impact Score, placing fourth.For Fauria, though, receiving production alone does not settle the argument. Gronkowski's ability to combine catching, route-running and blocking is what makes him the standard.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders' Trade Status Updated in New NFL Rumors Ahead of 1st Browns Start of 2026 Season
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns have "no plans" to move quarterback Shedeur Sanders ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns have "no plans" to move quarterback Shedeur Sanders ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

Sanders has sat behind Deshaun Watson on Cleveland's depth chart this season, although he's set to make his first start of the year against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday as Watson remains in concussion protocol.

Per Fowler, Sanders' upcoming start is "not a trade showcase."

The 24-year-old was initially selected by the Browns with a fifth-round pick in the 2025 NFL draft.

Sanders appeared in eight games as a rookie, including seven starts. He completed 56.6 percent of his throws for 1,400 yards and seven touchdowns to go along with 10 interceptions.

"Last year, I was able to see what I needed to see, feel different things during the games and understand what I need to get better at," Sanders said Wednesday, per ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi . "So, then going into this offseason, we worked on that, and training camp, of course, in this offseason, and overall, I'm just excited for the opportunity."

The Browns have exceeded expectations to open their 2026 campaign, as they own a 5-3 record through eight weeks.

Watson has started in each of Cleveland's first eight games, throwing for 1,806 yards and seven touchdowns while getting picked off three times. He's also rushed for 217 yards and one score.

Sanders will face a struggling New Orleans defense in his first start, as the team owns the NFL's No. 29 scoring defense by allowing 27.7 points per game. The Saints have also allowed opposing quarterbacks to post a 97.5 passer rating against them, ranking No. 23 among all teams (via Pro Football Reference ).

Kickoff between Cleveland and New Orleans on Sunday is at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: “I’m going to do whatever it takes to win": Patrick Mahomes willing to put his body on the line as Chiefs’ losing streak sparks desperate move
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes is ready to take a physical risk to help the Kansas City Chiefs solve their growing short-yardage problems.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes is ready to take a physical risk to help the Kansas City Chiefs solve their growing short-yardage problems. The quarterback has made it clear that he would not hesitate to run a quarterback sneak if it gave his team a better chance of winning. His comments come after Kansas City failed to score from the Denver Broncos’ one-yard line in a 28-24 loss, raising fresh questions about Andy Reid’s reluctance to use the play. Mahomes suffered a serious knee injury on a sneak in 2019, but that history has not changed his willingness to take the ball himself.Patrick Mahomes is ready to risk injury for the ChiefsThe Chiefs have avoided using Mahomes on quarterback sneaks since he dislocated his right kneecap against Denver in 2019. Reid has preferred other options, even when Kansas City needed only a yard to move the chains or reach the end zone.That approach came under renewed scrutiny after the Chiefs’ latest defeat. Kansas City held a 24-13 fourth-quarter lead but allowed Denver to score 15 unanswered points. The offense also had a chance to take the lead late in the game, only to struggle near the goal line.Mahomes did not hide his position when reporters asked about the possibility of running a sneak.“I'll just put it this way: I'm going to do whatever it takes to win,” he said. “At the end of the day, quarterback sneak, whatever that is, I'll do whatever it takes. It's not like I'm scared to go out there and put my body on the line.”The quarterback also acknowledged that his aggressive style has sometimes caused problems. Still, he believes the play deserves consideration if the Chiefs cannot find answers with their current options.The key distinction is that Mahomes is not asking to ignore his coach. He wants the team to make better decisions when the defense gives them a clear opening.Andy Reid’s play-calling faces fresh scrutinyThe controversy grew after Kansas City reached the Broncos’ one-yard line on a third-and-goal situation. Instead of asking Mahomes to sneak, Reid called a handoff to Kenneth Walker III. Denver’s defense stopped the running back before he could get moving.Mahomes explained that the play call was designed to get Walker downhill, but Denver’s defensive movement disrupted the plan. He also made clear that taking matters into his own hands would carry its own responsibility.“If I do call my own number, it's got to work,” Mahomes said.Reid has defended the Chiefs’ approach, saying the team has been successful without using quarterback sneaks. Mahomes, however, revealed that the play has remained in the game plan in certain situations. Kansas City can make changes at the line of scrimmage when the defensive formation allows it.That does not guarantee a change in the coming weeks. Mahomes is returning from knee surgery, and the Chiefs have reasons to protect their most important player. Yet the short-yardage struggles have made the decision harder to avoid.The Chiefs need more than a promise from their quarterback. They need a reliable way to finish drives. Mahomes has offered to take on the risk, but Reid must decide whether the potential reward is worth it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson has revealed that an unexplained neurological illness left him hospitalized for several days, raising fresh concerns about his health and recovery. The 24-year-old missed the Patriots’ November 1 win over the Miami Dolphins after the team placed him on the injured list with an illness. Henderson addressed the situation on Instagram on November 5, explaining that extensive medical tests had returned reassuring results, but doctors have yet to identify the cause of his symptoms. He also disclosed that the illness has affected his strength, coordination and physical functions.TreVeyon Henderson reveals unexplained neurological symptomsHenderson described the episode as an unexpected medical emergency that required several days of hospital care.“Recently, I experienced an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days,” he said.The running back underwent extensive testing and medical evaluations during his stay. While the results offered some relief, they have not provided a clear explanation for what happened.“During that time, I underwent extensive medical testing and evaluation. While the results of my comprehensive medical testing having come back positive and reassuring, the cause of this remains unknown and unexplainable,” Henderson continued.The distinction is important. Reassuring test results have not meant an immediate return to normal for the Patriots player. Henderson said the symptoms have affected several aspects of his physical ability, leaving him to work through the recovery process with medical professionals.He will “continue working closely with specialists and physical therapists” as he seeks to regain his health. The statement did not offer a timeline for his return to football.Henderson also made clear that his recovery is about more than getting back on the field. He is “committed to doing everything necessary to return to full health,” adding, “My health and long-term well-being remain my foremost priorities.”That message puts his immediate NFL future into perspective. With the cause of the illness still unknown, his focus remains on treatment and recovery rather than a specific return date.Patriots running back receives support during recoveryHenderson also thanked his wife, Mackenzie, who has been with him throughout the ordeal. The couple eloped shortly before the 2026 Super Bowl, and she has remained by his side as he deals with the medical uncertainty.He expressed gratitude to those who have supported him, including his family, the Patriots organization, his agent, medical team and teammates. Henderson also acknowledged the prayers and messages he has received from fans.The running back “respectfully” asked the public for “continued prayers and privacy as we focus on my health and recovery.”His request comes as concern grows over a player who had been a regular part of New England’s offense. Henderson was selected in the second round of the 2025 NFL Draft and appeared in all 21 of the Patriots’ regular-season and playoff games last year.That run included the team’s Super Bowl loss to the Seattle Seahawks. His ability to stay available throughout the season made his sudden absence against Miami a notable development.Henderson’s latest statement, however, offers no indication that he is close to returning. The Patriots have yet to provide a specific recovery timetable in the information shared, and the cause of his neurological symptoms remains unknown.For now, the most significant detail is that Henderson has received reassuring results from his medical tests, even as he continues to deal with symptoms that have affected his physical functions. His next steps involve working with specialists and physical therapists, with his long-term health taking priority over football.The uncertainty surrounding his condition remains, but Henderson has made his priorities clear. articles.title: Joe Milton QB1 Change Explained By Eagles' Nick Sirianni After Tanner McKee's Struggles
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni explained to reporters Friday why quarterback Joe Milton III will start in place of Tanner McKee on Sunday against the visiting New York Giants.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni explained to reporters Friday why quarterback Joe Milton III will start in place of Tanner McKee on Sunday against the visiting New York Giants.

"Obviously, that's always a difficult thing to think through, because it isn't ever just on one person. And matter of fact, I think Tanner played solid. But this is just what I felt like we needed to do right at this particular moment to give ourselves the best chance to win this weekend."

McKee has started the last three games in place of three-time Pro Bowler Jalen Hurts, who is out for the season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in his lungs.

The fourth-year quarterback and ex-Stanford star, who the Eagles selected with a sixth-round pick in the 2023 NFL draft, has completed 63.2 percent of his passes for 638 yards (5.6 yards per attempt), two touchdowns and two interceptions.

Philadelphia's offense hasn't gotten going, averaging just 15.0 points per game in a trio of losses to drop the Eagles to 2-6. In fairness to McKee, though, he's been placed in a tough spot with the Philadelphia offense so shorthanded this season.

Of note, running back Saquon Barkley (two games), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (four games) and tight end Dallas Goedert (two games) have all missed time due to injuries. Stalwart offensive tackle Lane Johnson retired after three games, and guard Landon Dickerson has played just three contests.

Now Milton will get a shot as the Eagles hope to end their four-game losing streak. Milton, a former Tennessee star and sixth-round pick in the 2024 NFL draft, has essentially played one full game in his career, and that was the final regular season game of the 2024 campaign.

He took over for New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye, who suffered a right hand injury, after the first drive and completed 22-of-29 passes for 241 yards and a touchdown while rushing for one more score in a 23-16 win over the Buffalo Bills, who played backups in the final week of the regular season in advance of the playoffs.

Milton saw a little action in four games for the Dallas Cowboys in 2025 after being traded there in April 2025. He completed 15-of-24 passes for 183 yards (7.6 yards per attempt), one touchdown and two picks.

Philadelphia claimed Milton off the Cowboys' practice squad in October, and now he has a great chance to firmly entrench himself as a QB1 and showcase his talents to the league.

articles.title: In 2007, Tom Brady became a father for the first time while preparing for another Super Bowl run; 16 years later, he walked away from the sport admitting his children were the only audience that had ever made him genuinely nervous
articles.summary: Tom Brady was 30 when his first child, Jack, was born on August 22, 2007, just weeks before the New England Patriots opened a season that would go 16-0.
articles.body: Tom Brady was 30 when his first child, Jack, was born on August 22, 2007, just weeks before the New England Patriots opened a season that would go 16-0. Sixteen years later, on February 1, 2023, Brady retired for good at 45, with seven Super Bowl rings. In between, he played in front of crowds of 70,000 and TV audiences of over 100 million. By his own telling, the audience that rattled him most sat at home, and it was his kids.How fatherhood and a Super Bowl chase collided in 2007Jack arrived on a quiet stretch of the calendar, between preseason games, to Brady and actress Bridget Moynahan. The two were no longer together by then, and Brady would marry Gisele Bündchen in 2009. So his first year as a dad did not look like a postcard. It looked like a quarterback learning two jobs at once.On the field, the Patriots were building something odd and brilliant. They added Randy Moss and Wes Welker, and Brady threw 50 touchdown passes, a league record at the time. New England won every regular-season game and every playoff game until Super Bowl XLII, where the Giants beat them 17-14 on February 3, 2008.That timing matters. Brady’s best statistical season and his most painful loss happened in the same months he was getting up for night feedings. Few athletes get a perfect year and a crushing ending wrapped around a life change that big. It is hard not to read the two as connected, even if Brady never framed it that way.Why a child’s stare was tougher than any stadiumTom Brady played in ten Super Bowls and won seven, more than any franchise has managed. He built his career on preparation. Film, routine, diet, repetition. A hostile crowd in Denver or Seattle was a problem with a solution, and he spent his whole working life finding those solutions.Children offer no such script. A teammate can be coached and a defense can be studied, but a seven-year-old watching from the stands is simply waiting to see how you handle a bad day. Brady has often said that losing was the thing that bothered him most. Now picture losing while your own kids watch, and then having to drive them home.That is the part of his story that gets overlooked. The nerves most players describe come from strangers, from the idea of failing in public. Brady’s version came from the opposite direction. The people who mattered most were the ones who would remember his mood after the game, not the score. Cameras forget fast. Kids do not.Raising three kids while still chasing ringsThe family grew along with the trophy case. Benjamin was born in December 2009 and Vivian in December 2012. Jack, Benjamin and Vivian became familiar faces at Patriots celebrations, and the Super Bowl wins after the 2014 and 2016 seasons often ended with Brady lifting a child as much as a trophy.By 2020, the Bradys had changed the whole map. At 42, Brady left New England for Tampa Bay, moved the household to Florida and won Super Bowl LV in his first season there. That win is the cleanest proof of his age-defying skill, but it also came with a hidden cost. Every extra year in the league meant another year of missed school events, birthday dinners and quiet weekends.The strain showed. Brady first retired on February 1, 2022, then reversed course 40 days later. In August he stepped away from Buccaneers camp for 11 days, citing personal matters. His divorce from Bündchen was finalized in October 2022. The Bucs finished the regular season 8-9 and lost to the Cowboys 31-14 in the wild-card round on January 16, 2023. It was a flat, honest ending for a man who had rarely allowed one.What the final retirement actually changedTom Brady made it official in a short video on February 1, 2023, exactly one year after his first attempt. This time, he said, it was for good. He left with 89,214 passing yards and 649 touchdown passes in the regular season, along with five Super Bowl MVP awards. His final season was far from his best, but it was enough to prove he could still play.The harder question was why he stopped when his body still allowed him to continue. Part of the answer is simple arithmetic. Jack was 15, Benjamin was 13 and Vivian was 10. Those are the years when a parent’s presence matters most and returns least, because teenagers rarely say thank you at the time.Brady did not disappear. He signed a deal with Fox Sports reported at 10 years and $375 million, and he became a minority owner of the Las Vegas Raiders, approved in October 2024. But both jobs are built around his schedule, not the other way around. He can leave a broadcast booth on Sunday night and be home before the kids wake up.That may be the quiet point of his exit. For two decades, his calendar belonged to the NFL. At 45, he handed it back to the three people who had watched every version of him, the winner and the loser, and who still had a vote in how his story ended.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk's Agent Gives Update After 49ers Meeting Amid NFL Reinstatement Attempt
articles.summary: Brandon Aiyuk's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, briefly discussed the wide receiver's meeting with the San Francisco 49ers on Friday.
articles.body:
Brandon Aiyuk's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, briefly discussed the wide receiver's meeting with the San Francisco 49ers on Friday.

"Hey, guys, to be continued," Rosenhaus told reporters, via Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area. "We don't have any further statements right now. But when we do, we'll let you know."

"We met with the bosses, man," Aiyuk said, per Maiocco. "Big bosses."

The 28-year-old was placed on the reserve/left squad list by the 49ers in Dec. 2025, but applied for reinstatement on Wednesday.

Aiyuk also provided an update on his health prior to the meeting.

"I'm feeling great, feeling healthy," Aiyuk told reporters. "It was a long recovery process, a long rehab process but I'm back to 100 percent and looking to get reinstated to the National Football League."

He has yet to appear in a game since suffering a torn ACL, MCL and meniscus in Oct. 2024.

Aiyuk signed a four-year contract extension worth $120 million with San Francisco ahead of the 2024 season, but Michael Silver of The Athletic reported that the team voided the guaranteed money in the wideout's deal after he "failed to attend meetings" and skipped "other team activities" following his knee injury.

ESPN's Nick Wagoner noted that Aiyuk turning in paperwork to be reinstated is the "first step" to forcing the 49ers to trade or release him.

He doesn't currently affect San Francisco's salary cap since he's on the reserve/left squad list, but the team would take on dead cap charges of $12.4 million in 2026 and $19.3 million in 2027 by releasing him (h/t Spotrac's Michael Ginnitti ).

The NFL has also informed Aiyuk that he needs to repay the 49ers roughly $13 million that he previously received in bonuses as he attempts to get reinstated.

He appeared in 69 games for San Francisco from 2020-24, recording 294 catches for 4,305 yards and 25 touchdowns.

articles.title: “There's no sense of urgency”: Tyreek Hill’s agent breaks silence on his return as he continues to recover from injuries
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill, the former Kansas City Chiefs’ wide receiver, seems to be waiting to get back on the field even though he has yet to be signed by a team in
articles.body: Tyreek Hill, the former Kansas City Chiefs’ wide receiver, seems to be waiting to get back on the field even though he has yet to be signed by a team in the league. As Tyreek Hill deals with rumors of a potential reunion with the Kansas City Chiefs, there have been serious concerns about his health. Amid this, his agent has opened up.Tyreek Hill’s agent opened up about the conversation he has had with the star playerA few weeks ago, Tyreek Hill’s agent Drew Rosenhaus made an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show where he said, "I am not pressuring Tyreek, nor am I setting a timeline for him…”Tyreek Hill’s agent Drew Rosenhaus added, “I think that what I've said to Tyreek is, 'Take your time. It's not when you come back, it's how you come back. We want you to come back when you feel your best.' There's no sense of urgency timing-wise."To this, the 32 year old free agent also took to his social media as he posted, "It’s almost time to get off the couch and get to work…”This has sparked widespread concern about Tyreek Hill’s health after the severe injuries he sustained in September of the last year.Tyreek Hill’s injury in the last season that changed the way his career was goingIn Week 4 of the last season, as the Miami Dolphins faced the New York Jets, Tyreek Hill sustained brutal injuries in the third quarter of the game.Tyreek Hill caught a 10 yard pass from the quarterback but as he was tackled out of bounds near the sideline by the New York Jets defender Malachi Moore, his left leg buckled under the contact, as he sustained a gruesome knee dislocation and multiple torn ligaments.In a scene that horrified fans, Tyreek Hill's cleat had to be cut off on the field so medical personnel could stabilize his leg.The star player seemed visibly in pain as he was carted off the field, taken directly to a local hospital, and stayed overnight for immediate medical testing and imaging.Since then, Tyreek Hill’s life took a turn and he has been facing issues, both in his personal and professional life.The 32 year old wide receiver was released by the Miami Dolphins in the next few weeks.For the unversed, Tyreek Hill was scheduled to carry a massive $51.1 million salary cap hit for the 2026 season. By moving on from him in February, the Miami Dolphins saved $22.8 million against the cap, providing the franchise with vital flexibility to restructure the team.Tyreek Hill has remained without a team since then. Even though rumors suggest that he could return to the Kansas City Chiefs, nothing has been finalised yet.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Insider Delivers Harsh Reality on Jaguars Trade Deadline Plans
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars are reportedly interested in adding a defensive tackle at the trade deadline. They are looking for a big-name addition that could mo...
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars are reportedly interested in adding a defensive tackle at the trade deadline. They are looking for a big-name addition that could move the needle, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. However, the market appears to be drying up in front of them, according to Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated.

Breer notes that the Jaguars were interested in Jeffery Simmons and DeForest Buckner, but being in the same division as both hurt their odds of making a move.

He goes on to mention that the other options around the league that are big names are not as likely to be moved.

"Washington's Daron Payne was drawing interest before he got hurt," noted Breer. "To this point, the Eagles have said no to teams on Moro Ojomo (more on him in a bit), and the Dolphins have done the same with Zach Sieler. The pie-in-the-sky swing for someone to take, in the Simmons aftermath, might be for Panthers star Derrick Brown. That would be very expensive, though, with Carolina not actively looking to move him."

So, the next four names that are worth targeting for the Jaguars appear to either be off the table or at a price range that is hard to reach.

Jacksonville Jaguars Remain in Pursuit of Defensive Lineman at Trade Deadline

Breer added that there are a few lower-end names that are coming up as options for the Jaguars.

"Grover Stewart's an option, with the Saints' Davon Godchaux and Nathan Shepherd, Patriots' Christian Barmore and Panthers' Bobby Brown III others who've come up in trade talks," added Breer.

However, those names do not move the needle in the way that Ojomo, Brown or Sieler would. It is worth noting that John Shipley of Jaguars OnSI thinks that their most recent win is going to cause the team to meet the Panthers' demands and pay up for a big name.

"I think the Jaguars will add two defenders by the end of the deadline," wrote Shipley after the Jags' Week 9 win. "My best guess is that it comes at the defensive tackle and safety positions, though edge is always a spot to watch due to the depth of pass-rushers who could be had. My ultimate guess is they add Derrick Brown."

While safety is also an option, all of the smoke continues to build at nose tackle.

The Jaguars' defensive line was always a problem, and the team was looking for help before Week 8. However, in Week 8, they lost their best run defender and top nose tackle, DaVon Hamilton. With Hamilton out, the Jags went from exploring options to being all-in on adding a big name.

The team does not play another game before the trade deadline. They get to see how teams fare this weekend while they prepare to make a move. The deadline is Tuesday, November 10.

articles.title: NFL Draft big board 2.0: While Jeremiah Smith is No. 1, Arch Manning remains in top 10 trailing Drew Mestemaker
articles.summary: Ohio State's star wideout remains a gravity-shifter, and Manning's traits are too hard to dismiss despite his struggles.
articles.body:
Here's an updated NFL Draft big board as the league approaches its midseason mark and we enter the home stretch of the college football regular season with the playoffs to follow. The conundrum on the timing of this big board is that so many players, especially quarterbacks, could return to school or transfer. This makes me hesitant on how high to put players who could very well be on this board in a year's time after returning to campus (or transferring to another campus).

I'm assuming the players are all declaring for the purposes of this board. With the ever-changing environment of college football and ever-moving targets of player evaluation, we have bob and weave with it.

Here's more than half-a-hundred names now that we're about halfway home in a wild college football season that has made for a very interesting draft class.

A force of nature at receiver, Smith has been a standout player and absurdly productive at every level of his career. He is strong, explosive and has an excellent build that allows him to bounce off tackles and constantly eat up yards after the catch. His power makes him dangerous on inbreakers that allow him to build up speed and get downhill in a hurry, and his speed and burst out of breaks make him dangerous coming out of routes. Smith is a gravity-shifter and true math-changer for the offense and for the defense to account for. It's hard to compare any athlete to Julio Jones, and welp, here we are with Smith. At worst you're looking at a Josh Gordon-like player.

A long athlete with range and advanced feel for the position, Moore affects a lot of throws with his length, and amplifies it with his body positioning. He has the speed to run with faster wideouts, and the hand-eye coordination and timing to constantly make plays on the football. He showed those skills immediately as a true freshman starter in South Bend. He shines when asked to shadow better WRs and remains an impact player when aligning in the slot. Moore has a chance to be one of the best cornerback prospects I've ever studied.

A long, lean athlete with agility and Gumby-like bend, Stewart can move around blocks in ways that few can. He still needs refinement with how he uses his hands, but he has a wingspan like a pterodactyl to stave off blockers, and flashes violent stabs and slaps that would unlock a whole new level with more consistency. Stewart's get-off and twitchiness make him dangerous off the edge or on games as either a penetrator or looper. He's what teams look for at this position.

An easy mover with length and pop with his hands, Seaton can latch on and dominate defenders in the run game. He still has work to do with his hand placement, but Seaton has improved in his polish, eye awareness and overall technique, especially in pass protection. Seaton has the twitch and size to be a valid blindside protector at the next level.

Much will be made about Mestemaker's lack of experience as a starting quarterback at any level (he was a backup in high school and then a walk-on at North Texas). Despite not having the experience or snaps that other typically highly touted quarterbacks have, Mestemaker seems to know how to play the position. He has a good arm that can access all parts of the field and is willing to push the ball from muddy pockets. He can change arm slots and layer the football up and over defenders when needed. Mestemaker is tall and has a long frame that he has started to fill out. He is a solid athlete, albeit not an overwhelming one. But he has a loose arm, is very good at avoiding sacks despite his lack of experience, and can consistently throw on the move, even when working left. Mestemaker is willing to move and work from the pocket and has enough giddyup to work outside of it, too. He has had some inconsistent performances the past few weeks with his decision-making, plays in a very conducive offense that can make his eyes lock in a bit too much (he has yet to take an under-center snap, not a damning thing but worth noting), and hasn't played the toughest competition so far this season. But Mestemaker has the ability to create throws within and out of structure, and has the size (6-foot-3, 215 pounds) and enough arm to translate to the next level.

Simmons is an explosive athlete who is asked to do everything for Texas' defense. He has shined while pinning his ears back and getting after the passer. He wins with a quick first step and has the ability to run the hoop and turn a corner on offensive tackles. He has been asked to drop into coverage in his college career, and also mirror athletic quarterbacks on passing downs, showing off the front-seven versatility modern defenses love. Simmons' agility and speed shine in these other areas.

An outside receiver with size (6-foot-4, 208 pounds) and long speed, Becker burst onto the scene in a talented wide receiver room and was constantly coming down with big catches in big moments. Becker has strong hands and excellent hand-eye coordination in catching range that allows him to frequently come down with the football. He has long legs, but also shows enough quickness and bend to run a fully developed route tree, which raises his ceiling.

Manning's 2026 season has been a journey of ups and downs . He still displays the size (6-foot-4, 222 pounds), athleticism, pocket movement and willingness to push the ball that make for an intriguing prospect. That willingness to push the ball, even in too-often mucky pockets, leads to exciting plays but also game-swinging negative ones, too. Manning's results haven't always set the world on fire, but he has a style that translates to the next level, namely that aggression and lack of fear throwing into tight windows or tight pockets. When grouped with his speed and arm, he makes for a still-intriguing package at quarterback. More consistent results will help it all feel better. Manning still has to learn to take an easier answer quicker, which to me is to use his legs and rushing ability more often, something he's tapped back into in recent weeks. His process, while far from perfect, is cleaner when reviewing it on film, especially amid a frustrating Texas offensive ecosystem.

Williams is an easy-moving athlete who gets better each week. This former basketball player is an older prospect, but he is still tapping into his potential because of his relative lack of experience at the position and football altogether. He has twitchiness, foot speed and length to develop into a longtime blindside protector. There is also enough strength to be an asset in the run game.

Cole has sideline-to-sideline range, which isn't hyperbolic as he actually displays it. He plays with his hair on fire, has the range to cover large swaths of the middle of the field, and shows an ability to come forward in the run game and as a blitzer. Cole's versatility and four-down ability is what a modern linebacker looks like.

Hampton is a big and long corner who can play in zone and impact the game with his size (6-foot-2, 205 pounds) and awareness, but might actually be most unlocked as a player in man coverage situations. He is not overly twitchy, yet he's a smooth athlete who can fluidly get in and out of his turns. His size, foot speed and ball skills give him a chance at being a lockdown player on the outside at the next level. He reminds me a bit of James Bradberry.

Note: Simmons has reportedly "re-signed" with Missouri for the 2027 season on Friday, but with a caveat that he can still explore the draft after the season. I have kept his ranking and report as is.

Simmons can simply spin the football. His aggression, arm talent and weekly improvement has his stock soaring, even if the box score doesn't always indicate that. Simmons is a redshirt junior but will turn just 21 soon. Simmons wants to win from the pocket and might not tap into his creativity as quickly as he should, but his high-end throws are as good as you'll ever see. Simmons has the willingness to attack all areas and a feel for ball placement that keeps all windows alive with his top-shelf arm talent, and his arm and timing will allow that to translate nicely to the NFL. He is still young and has to show the ability to stay consistent when under pressure, but Simmons has put together some of the strongest tape at the position, despite the lack of points for Missouri's offense at times.

Echoles is a uniquely built (6-foot-3, 315 pounds) but powerful player who flashes quick hands to win early and stays active throughout the rep. He has good pop when engaging blockers and can anchor down in the run game. Echoles is young (just turned 20 in August). He can stay on the field for all four downs and fill a variety of roles, with disruptive play and a unique combination of bulk, strength and quick feet.

He's a disruptive defender who is asked to play all across OU's defensive line. Stone will play a chunk of snaps at nose tackle, but I think his best snaps are when he gets to play as a defensive end. He is strong, constantly keeps his feet upon contact, and can eat and split double-teams in the run game. His versatility works in his favor, as his varied skills let him be a valid player at any spot. He's also a nice option to use on stunts and twists. Stone battled injuries early this season, but he has shown off his ability to impact games even if it doesn't always show up in the box score.

Harris is a big, fluid receiver who can win vertically on the outside and has the route-running feel to beat zone when aligned inside. He has strong hands and can win consistently in contested catch situations, and is agile enough to create yards after the catch on in-breaking routes and underneath touches. I'm a big fan of Harris' game.

Chambliss rocks. But he's going to be a knotty prospect for teams to unravel as I have to acknowledge his older age (turned 24 in August) and lack of ideal size (6-foot, 205 pounds). Despite being a short QB in NFL terms, Chambliss has good bulk and is excellent working from the pocket. The ball is constantly out on time and he has shown off the ability to work tight windows and between the numbers. His strong throwing style gets highlighted in the red zone. Chambliss has a strong arm and can get the RPMs to drive the football, even from awkward platforms and tight pockets. Despite being a good athlete, he is a keen and capable operator from the pocket who looks to scramble only as a last resort. I have likened his size and game to former NFL QB Jeff Garcia.

Johnson is just one of those players who boosts his teammates around him as a solidifying force with his smarts and sound play. He has athleticism and pop to his blocks, too. Johnson has positional versatility, but I think his best spot long-term will be at center.

A disruptive interior lineman who can win instantly against the run or pass, Moten fires off the snap and constantly stays low and plays with quick and violent hands. Even when not winning with his first strike, Moten does a nice job of attempting a second move to win as a pass rusher. He has the size, quickness, explosiveness, with some versatility, too, to appeal to any defense.

19. LaNorris Sellers, QB, South Carolina

He's a ridiculous runner and playmaker with the football. Sellers has a high-end arm that he can access from all platforms and is an excellent athlete with size (6-foot-3, 240 pounds). He showed consistency from the pocket in 2025 and this season, despite said pockets constantly being obliterated. Sellers has continued to mitigate sacks and negative plays with his otherworldly athleticism, strength and balance.

He hasn't had a lot of help with his surroundings at South Carolina, often having to pull a rabbit out of a hat just to throw the ball away because his protection broke down AND no one could get open. He is not a total wild horse, though; his decisions to scramble and improvise make sense. He will have the occasional spray, but I also think his calmer sense of play has led to improvements in accuracy, with an understanding of when to use touch on his throws. And he gets rid of the ball in a timely manner when the pocket is clean (and has shown a better understanding of when to throw the ball away), a trait that has shown up in areas like the red zone this year.

I had said before I was giving Sellers until Halloween to see how his consistency had improved and whether he was worth continuing to buy into despite a lack of consistent results (he was a top-10 prospect before the season). His uptick in overall decisiveness over the past month has me very encouraged, even if there is still a lack of depth to what he is asked to run in Kendal Briles' offense. I'm continuing to buy into an exciting player who has more polish to his game than you'd expect, but still needs more refinement.

Siani started on the right side to begin this season in Austin, but kicked over to the left tackle when teammate Trevor Goosby suffered an injury (Siani played at left tackle at Wake Forest too). He is still cleaning up his hand usage and his pad level can get too high at times, but he has the freaky bend and light feet to recover whenever he gets out of position. He also brings some real pop when he connects in the run game. Siani is still relatively new to football, but his athleticism in such a large frame has me betting on his upside.

Heard is a mammoth left tackle (6-foot-6, 325 pounds) who uses his size to his benefit. He will get after it in the run game, but is a surprisingly fluid mover in space as a puller, climbing to the second level, and when working horizontally. His hands usage can be inconsistent, and like most bigger linemen he can get caught playing too upright. He still manages to have winning reps because of his strength, tenacity and that surprising athleticism.

Here's a bowling ball who knocks bodies around on the inside. Gilliam can win instantly with his quickness and strong hands that can get under blockers because of his stout frame (6-foot-2, 305 pounds). He's been a standout on a very fun Tennessee defense.

Marsh has strong hands, and very good body control and balance. He's very quarterback friendly as a pass catcher and has a knack for finding soft spots against zone. And he's an excellent blocker. He's a useful and reliable player who can operate inside and outside. I especially like him as a power slot at the next level to highlight his blocking and route-running feel.

Robinson is a twitchy athlete with length and ball skills. He's improved a ton this year in his technique and eye discipline. His awareness and burst let him quickly recognize and close on underneath throws, too.

Baugh is a big back (6-foot-1, 225 pounds) but has the quickness and twitchiness of a much smaller athlete. He runs with balance and constantly does a nice job of setting up his blocks at the second level. Baugh doesn't have overwhelming long speed, but does have burst to get north in a hurry. He is a natural catcher of the football and has the size to hold up in pass protection, giving him every-down value. Just a cool player.

The former Legion of Boom coaches will drool over Jones, a tall (6-foot-4) and long outside cornerback who is constantly asked to work between high-low concepts on the outside. Jones has long speed to go with his size, too. He constantly is able to stay vertical with receivers and keep up with them on crossing routes. It's not all perfect, but just a little more refinement and Jones can show off an exciting combination of tools and real football ability.

Traore plays with strong hands and can affect the run and pass with his ability to strike and push the pocket. He isn't the longest player, but he knows how to use his length. Those skills, combined with the burst and aggressiveness he plays with, make him a tough player to block. He's even flashed some successful spin moves this season. There's some Jared Verse to his game.

Johnson has excellent ball skills and the ability to stretch the field. He's not overly explosive but plays with balance and coordination. He also has some blocking chops, even if it's not always perfect. He can come down with contested catches, has a knack for working himself into friendly spots for the quarterback, and can pick up some yards after the catch as well.

It's not a shock that Green is a basketball player along with being a jumbo-sized (6-foot-7, 242 pounds) tight end. He is built like a power forward, but fluid and quick enough as a route-runner and athlete that LSU would split him out and isolate him as a receiver. He is constantly winning his routes and creating yards after the catch. His size and ball skills also make him an obvious asset in the red zone. Green has battled a knee injury this year, but came back recently and was productive.

Johnson is a long and rangy athlete who can cover ground easily with his bouncy strides. He can play in the deep spot but Notre Dame rotates him down as a buzz defender to be near the box constantly. Johnson is willing to come down from depth to close in the run game and is an effective blitzer and overall tackler. Just watch last year's Pitt game to see what Johnson is capable of: he jumps a route for a pick-6, then follows it up on the next drive with a sack on a blitz and a tackle on the running back from depth. Johnson has been hurt for essentially the whole season with a foot injury, but it's hard to dismiss his intriguing combination of athleticism and intelligence.

A tough finisher in the run game who is light on his feet, Lauck plays quick with good awareness for what defenses are attempting to do on each play. This allows him to move fast as a run blocker and pass protector. He can get caught playing too high in pass protection, which makes him vulnerable to longer pass rushers, but he shows good, patient hands.

Cheeks is a twitchy edge rusher with surprising pop when he goes from speed to power. He is a competitive player who is constantly attacking tackles on every snap. His energy and ability to hold up in the run game — with the athleticism and agility to turn the corner and get after the passer — make him an enjoyable watch.

Lopa has been one of the biggest risers this season, not only because he's been productive in terms of interceptions, but he's a unique player with elite size and versatility at safety (he's listed at 6-foot-5 and lines up in the slot and in the box at times). He would be an exciting defensive backfield weapon to deploy for more creative play-callers and would help defenses go toe-to-toe with the tight ends and bigger slot players that NFL offenses are currently deploying.

Pierre is a relentless pass rusher who can also set the edge in the run game and drop into coverage when needed. He has developed his pass rush plan this year, and has shown more strength against the run.

Harris is a long, springy receiver who shows inside-outside ability because of his easy movement ability, catching range and willingness to scrap inside. He has strong hand-eye coordination that makes him a vertical threat, and Harris has enough agility to turn and pick up yards on underneath routes despite his long legs. He reminds me of a Diet Coke version of Tetairoa McMillan.

Coleman is an exciting package of size, twitch and length to be a starting outside receiver who can stretch the field and attack all three levels. But he has been maddeningly inconsistent this year, with brutal drops and a lack of feel and awareness, which especially shows up as a blocker. There's still a lot of talent here, but Coleman needs a stronger, and more consistent, final stretch of the season to get his stock moving in the other direction.

37. Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa, LB, Notre Dame

He's a hammerhead linebacker who flashes every game as a run defender and as a blitzer. Viliamu-Asa can blow up blockers and ball carriers on contact and is best when working downhill. He has shown off range to hold up in coverage, too.

Moore is a calm operator. He has good arm strength and is a good athlete who can throw consistently on the move. You can tell that Moore has really focused on his footwork and how to work through passing plays during his time at Oregon, and he constantly found good answers to the problems defenses showed him and tried to stay on time with the play.

There were times I wished Moore would push the ball a bit on high-low concepts in 2025, and I was still left wanting more when he played in 2026 before suffering a brutal hit and concussion. He too often defers to the "safer" of two options on a concept, and he missed throws early this year on shot plays and in the red zone. Moore is a complicated evaluation. There was a clear ascension in play in 2025, and he can be a really accurate thrower with sound timing when he's feeling in rhythm. But his overall play stagnated at the end of the year and into a chunk of 2026 before his injury. He could return to school, transfer or declare and I would understand each choice.

Mensah has been über-productive in his first year for the Hurricanes. He is a sharp processor who maximizes his below-average arm strength with his timing and ball placement. Mensah benefits from a quarterback-friendly environment against a weak schedule, but shows off the ability to maximize his opportunities. More often than not the ball is going to the right spot at the right time. He has average size (6-foot-3, 205 pounds) and is a solid athlete who can run when needed, but prefers to do his work from the pocket. There's some Kirk Cousins to his game in terms of accuracy, clean throwing mechanics and footwork, and total understanding of the offense. But he lacks the upper-echelon arm or creation ability.

Carr is a smart player who understands the intent of every play that Notre Dame calls. He shows off an advanced understanding of the offense and operation, often changing up cadences and making play changes before the snap. He has the willingness to push the football when needed but lacks high-end tools in terms of size (6-foot-2, 215 pounds) and athleticism. He has a solid arm that he maximizes with his timing. His accuracy can waver under pressure or when having to consistently create, and his advanced understanding of the game can be a double-edged sword when evaluating him, in terms of how much more there is to tap into given his more-or-less average tools.

articles.title: San Francisco 49ers Announce Christian McCaffrey Decision Before Raiders Game
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers are 6-1 entering Week 9 of the NFL season as they prepare to take on the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Following Friday’s practice, th...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers are 6-1 entering Week 9 of the NFL season as they prepare to take on the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday.

Following Friday's practice, the team provided several key injury updates and officially ruled out veteran wide receivers Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Christian Kirk, leaving the 49ers offense quite shorthanded.

However, they also received positive injury news on star running back Christian McCaffrey, who sustained a mild hamstring injury the last time San Francisco took the field in Week 7.

In positive news, McCaffrey will be good to go for Sunday's contest after the 49ers officially removed him from the injury report. He logged back-to-back practices on Thursday and Friday.

McCaffrey has played in every game this season and continues to serve as a workhorse in Kyle Shanahan's high-powered offense. He'll likely have to shoulder an even greater workload this week with the WR corps so depleted.

Earlier this week, McCaffrey revealed that he was caught off guard when he learned the injury was a hamstring issue, but said he "feels great."

"I had no idea [it was a hamstring injury]," McCaffrey said Wednesday. "Sometimes the adrenaline and all these other things can get to you… It wasn't too bad. Having the bye week was awesome. But now I feel great."

McCaffrey has appeared in all seven games, recording 84 carries for 389 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. He's also caught 34 passes for 251 yards.

He's in his 11th NFL season and fifth with the 49ers after San Francisco acquired him from the Carolina Panthers in 2022 in exchange for four draft picks.

Another positive sign for the 49ers is that they'll welcome back star pass rusher Nick Bosa, who has missed several games this season with a calf strain he sustained during practice.

Bosa will line up alongside DeForest Buckner, who will make his first start with the 49ers since San Francisco acquired him from the Indianapolis Colts during the bye week.

articles.title: Eagles release RB Dameon Pierce with injury settlement
articles.summary: The Eagles have released running back Dameon Pierce with an injury settlement, ending his stint in Philadelphia after he was placed on injured reserve
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles have parted ways with another running back, releasing Dameon Pierce with an injury settlement as the team continues to deal with injuries and uncertainty at the position. According to NFL Communications , Philadelphia reached an injury settlement with Pierce on Friday, ending his brief stint with the organization less than two weeks after placing him on injured reserve.

Pierce appeared in three games for Philadelphia, recording 96 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 37 carries. The former Houston Texans running back had emerged as an important contributor amid the Eagles ' mounting injuries before suffering an undisclosed injury during the fourth quarter of Philadelphia's Week 7 loss to the Dallas Cowboys.

The Eagles placed Pierce on injured reserve Oct. 28, promoting former Dallas Cowboys running back Jaydon Blue from the practice squad to take his spot on the active roster.

Dameon Pierce's brief Eagles tenure ends

Philadelphia initially signed Pierce to its practice squad before the regular season began, giving the team an experienced option behind Saquon Barkley. The Eagles promoted Pierce to the active roster Oct. 7 after placing Tank Bigsby on injured reserve. With Barkley battling injuries and Will Shipley also sidelined, Pierce provided a physical running presence and became part of Philadelphia's backfield rotation.

Pierce originally entered the NFL as a fourth-round pick by Houston in the 2022 NFL Draft. He rushed for 939 yards and four touchdowns as a rookie, establishing himself as a productive downhill runner before injuries and changes to the Texans' backfield reduced his role.

His opportunity in Philadelphia came during a difficult stretch for the Eagles, who have struggled to establish a consistent rushing attack despite entering the season with significant expectations.

The injury settlement allows Pierce and the Eagles to move forward separately rather than keeping the running back on injured reserve for the remainder of his recovery.

What's next for Eagles' running back rotation?

Philadelphia enters Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the New York Giants with Barkley continuing to manage hamstring and back injuries. The veteran was limited during Friday's practice but did not receive a game-day injury designation.

Blue remains on the active roster and provides additional depth, while Elijah Mitchell has been available as a practice squad option. The Eagles are also awaiting the return of injured running backs Bigsby and Shipley.

The running game remains a significant concern for an offense averaging just 17.1 points and 265.3 total yards per game. Philadelphia has struggled to consistently create running lanes, sustain drives, and generate explosive plays during its six-game losing streak.

Pierce's departure removes another experienced option from the backfield, although his placement on injured reserve had already taken him out of the immediate rotation.

The Eagles will host the Giants on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at Lincoln Financial Field before entering their Week 10 bye, hoping to establish a more productive rushing attack with Joe Milton III making his first start at quarterback.

articles.title: 49ers' ‘Hulk' was a zero-star recruit. Now he's manhandling NFL linemen
articles.summary: Five years after being thrust into the spotlight at an FCS school, Sebastian Valdez, a 2025 undrafted free agent, is a 6-foot-3, 301-pound regular for the Sa...
articles.body:
In 2021, an 18-year-old Sebastian Valdez traversed up I-15 North to depart his hometown of Spring Valley for a much less familiar place called Bozeman, Montana. Uncertainty hung in the air. He was set to begin his freshman season at Montana State with a new head coach, a new defensive coordinator and a new position coach - none of whom recruited him to the school.

Shawn Howe, the Bobcats' first-year defensive line coach, scanned his new group of players at one of the team's first organized practices. Among them, a scrawny, zero-star freshman edge rusher immediately popped. It was Valdez.

Right then and there, Howe forecasted the young man's future.

"That's the next 3-technique (defensive tackle) at Montana State," Howe, now a defensive assistant with the Pittsburgh Steelers, recalled thinking.

Even if Valdez didn't know it at the time, Howe was right. And even though Howe was right, the moment came a little sooner than either of them could have envisioned. During the first week of the season, one of Montana State's starting defensive tackles blew out his knee.

That's when Howe called Valdez into his office. "Hey, we're gonna move you to D-tackle," he said, "and you're the future of this position."

In that moment, Valdez recalled, anxiety bubbled. He had a lot of questions. But he wasn't going to turn back now.

"He just laid out this whole vision for me, and I just trusted him," Valdez told the Chronicle on Thursday. "And yeah, the rest is history."

Five years after being thrust into the spotlight at a Football Championship Subdivision school, Valdez, a 2025 undrafted free agent, is a 6-foot-3, 301-pound rotation regular for the San Francisco 49ers . The 24-year-old defensive tackle earned his first standard NFL contract last month after spending more than a year toiling on the 49ers' practice squad. In five career games, he has recorded nine tackles, three quarterback hits, two tackles-for-loss and a sack. And most importantly, he looks like he belongs.

What have Valdez's teammates, who dubbed him "The Hulk" because of his immense strength, thought of his play so far? One teammate offered a three-word response.

"Manhandling dudes, bro," fellow defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa said.

In a league full of underdog stories, Valdez owns one of extreme proportions.

Unlike most NFL players, Valdez never dreamed of this life as a kid. He didn't play football until sixth grade. He was a no-star recruit out of Monte Vista High School in Southern California, where he also wrestled for three years and won a CIF state championship. In fact, Valdez said, "there was a point in high school that I enjoyed wrestling more than football."

Despite his success on the mat, he earned no collegiate wrestling offers. He did receive one in football, though, so he informed his parents - both Mexican immigrants - of his intentions to attend Montana State on a scholarship. Jesús and Norah Valdez struggled to grasp the concept.

"My parents never even, like - they didn't even understand how football works," Valdez said. "They didn't understand that I was gonna go away for school and that it was free."

They eventually understood, and Valdez went off to Bozeman for his freshman campaign under a new and unfamiliar coaching staff. He played "pretty solid" as a fill-in defensive tackle as a freshman, he said, yet there was one problem.

In order to play defensive tackle, he needed to add weight. And a lot of it.

Howe instructed Valdez, weighing around 235 pounds at the time, to eat like crazy, but in a controlled manner. "He didn't want me getting, like, fat," Valdez deadpanned. So, what did he eat to remain in an extreme caloric surplus as a college student living in the middle of Montana?

"Oh, man," Valdez said with a chuckle. "It was chicken and rice, chicken and rice. I can't even eat chicken and rice anymore. … It was just constantly that.

"Even my roommates would see me with a little scale to weigh food, and they were kind of like, 'What are you doing? ' And I was just like, 'Man, trust. Like, I got to do this.' And it worked out. Gained the weight the right way. My speed, my strength got better … I think my second year I was like 265 (pounds)."

Valdez spent three seasons in Bozeman. He played his senior campaign at the University of Washington, which offered a steep increase in competition. Valdez didn't exactly produce: two sacks and 4½ tackles for loss in 13 games. But he spent the better part of that year playing through an elbow injury that forced him to "walk on eggshells," according to Jason Kaufusi, Washington's defensive line coach, and damaged his draft stock.

Valdez failed to earn a 2025 draft combine invite. Instead, his freakish athletic traits popped at the Huskies' on-campus pro day. Niners guard Carver Willis, who had just transferred from Kansas State to Washington, attended the event. He recalled being in awe while watching Valdez bench press 225 pounds 34 times (which would have led all players at the combine) and run the 40-yard dash in under 5 seconds.

"He basically looked like the UW Hulk," Willis said. "I was like, 'Oh, this guy's a dude .'"

He signed with the 49ers - largely because of how he fit into their scheme - as a free agent. As a rookie, he sat idly on the 49ers' practice squad. Head coach Kyle Shanahan elevated him to the active roster for multiple games last season, not with the intention to play him but rather as a "reward" for his hard work.

At that point, San Francisco almost lost Valdez to the Steelers, who wanted to sign him off San Francisco's practice squad. But Valdez opted against it, explaining that "the vision that the 49ers had for me - and I think the vision I had for myself with this team - was a lot greater than what I had with the Steelers." He added that Pittsburgh's' "read attack" system doesn't suit him as well.

Said Shanahan: "He was someone we really gambled with. It was someone we were very nervous about losing. We feel lucky that we didn't because he was playing at that level" while on the practice squad.

In 2026, after a strong preseason, Valdez again didn't make the cut for the 53-man roster. Sensing a theme here? Earning football respect has never come easy for Valdez.

"It's been like that every year with me," he said. "I gotta work for everything I have in my life. It's not a surprise to me."

Was he beginning to doubt himself? He claims not.

"It was only a matter of time," Valdez said, "whether it was here or somewhere else. I didn't want to go into a hole mentally. I just wanted to stay true to myself and still come in, have a routine and practice the way I practice, and I knew things would work out eventually."

Odighizuwa shared a similar message with the second-year player at that point: "I'm like, 'Don't stop working. I know you're not going to, but like, especially with how things are going around here (with the injuries). … Your opportunity is right around the corner.'"

Odighizuwa was right. After nearly every defensive tackle ahead of him got hurt, Valdez got his chance. He impressed enough in San Francisco's Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals to earn a spot on the active roster.

And on Oct. 11 against the Seattle Seahawks, Valdez had his moment.

Late in the first quarter, Valdez churned his legs on the Lumen Field turf. He extended his arms through the chest of left guard Grey Zabel. His first move didn't do much, so he crossed to the left, then to the right, then to the left again. His pure power overmatched his counterpart. Zabel relented. Valdez knocked quarterback Sam Darnold onto his back, crashing to the ground with him before rising up and letting out a passionate roar.

The roar signaled that Valdez, after taking a long, winding road, had finally arrived. Even though Valdez's salary cap hit ($844,167) remains the lowest on the 49ers' roster, what do his parents think now about his profession?

"Now they're super proud," he said, "and they understand the game of football."
