articles.title: WR Brandon Aiyuk says he's 'back to 100%' and hoping for reinstatement ahead of meeting at 49ers facility
articles.summary: San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan said he 'could(n't) care less' about the situation.
articles.body:
Brandon Aiyuk is back in the San Francisco 49ers' facility, four months after he vowed to never set foot in the building again.

Aiyuk, who has not played since October 2024 following a lengthy recovery from ACL and MCL tears, has also seen his career affected by an off-field feud with the team . After a year-long saga, the wide receiver finally returned to Santa Clara with agent Drew Rosenhaus in order to negotiate his reinstatement to the team at the Niners' business offices.

"I'm feeling great, feeling healthy. It was a long recovery process, a long rehab process, but I'm back to 100 percent and looking to get reinstated into the National Football League," Aiyuk said, via David Lombardi of the San Francisco Standard .

When asked, Aiyuk did not clarify whether he planned to return to the 49ers or hoped for the team to release him so he could pursue other opportunities.

However, if he does want to return to San Francisco, that bridge appears to have been burned. When asked about the situation in a news conference on Friday, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said that he had "no clue" what would happen with the meeting.

"Could [ sic ] care less," Shanahan said of the situation.

After the meeting, Rosenhaus told reporters that they did not have any additional updates, though Aiyuk said that they met with the "big bosses," via NBC Sports' Matt Maiocco .

To add to the drama, multiple reporters said that there were police officers outside of the facility ahead of Aiyuk's meeting. That presence came amid additional reports that an arrest warrant for Aiyuk , related to a speeding incident outside Levi's Stadium in December 2025, was still active.

Aiyuk's meeting at the 49ers' facility was another chapter in a lengthy, bitter saga between the receiver and his team. Last November, San Francisco voided Aiyuk's guarantees in the wake of an increasingly strained relationship with the 28-year-old wideout.

By January, general manager John Lynch was saying Aiyuk had played his final snap in a Niners uniform. That also appears to be something Aiyuk wants as well, as the receiver spent the summer publicly asking San Francisco to cut him.

On Wednesday, Aiyuk turned in his reinstatement paperwork , starting the process of his return to the team. The move came just a few days after the receiver hired Rosenhaus to help him launch his comeback.

The receiver will now hope San Francisco will release him so he can sign with a new team. However, Aiyuk reportedly also owes the Niners around $13 million in bonus forfeiture , though the NFL Management Council and NFL Players Association are reportedly trying to find a resolution.

articles.title: Ravens waive QB Austin Reed, finalize Jacoby Brissett trade
articles.summary: The Ravens waived quarterback Austin Reed after finalizing their trade for Jacoby Brissett, reshaping Baltimore's quarterback depth chart
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens continue to overhaul their quarterback room, waiving Austin Reed after officially completing their trade with the Arizona Cardinals for veteran Jacoby Brissett. According to NFL Communications , Baltimore waived Reed on Friday as the organization finalized the acquisition of Brissett, who is expected to become the Ravens ' fourth starting quarterback in four games when they face the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 10.

The transaction comes one day after Baltimore suffered a 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, extending its losing streak to four games and dropping Jesse Minter's team to 4-5.

Reed had been part of Baltimore's emergency quarterback depth following injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. Still, Brissett's arrival gives offensive coordinator Declan Doyle a more experienced option as the Ravens attempt to revive their struggling offense.

Ravens finalize Jacoby Brissett trade with Cardinals.

Baltimore officially completed its trade with Arizona on Friday, acquiring Brissett and a 2027 fifth-round draft pick in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round selection and a 2028 seventh-round pick. The Ravens also received financial assistance from Arizona, which converted a portion of Brissett's remaining salary into a signing bonus before completing the deal.

Brissett, 33, brings 73 career starts and 11 seasons of NFL experience to a Baltimore offense that has struggled since losing Jackson and Huntley.

The veteran started Arizona's first eight games this season before being replaced by Gardner Minshew II. His availability made him an attractive option for a Ravens team that suddenly found itself relying on inexperienced quarterbacks during an important stretch of the season.

Baltimore has now scored fewer than 14 points in four consecutive games for the first time in franchise history.

Austin Reed becomes latest Ravens quarterback departure

Reed joined Baltimore's quarterback options after Jackson suffered a right thumb injury and Huntley sustained a toe injury during the Ravens' Week 8 loss to Buffalo.

Both quarterbacks subsequently landed on injured reserve, leaving rookie Joe Fagnano and newly signed Kedon Slovis among Baltimore's available options.

Fagnano made his first NFL start Thursday against Jacksonville but struggled to establish a passing attack, completing 10 of 18 attempts for 60 yards and two interceptions. He finished with a 22.7 passer rating as the Ravens managed just 10 points.

Reed's departure reduces the number of quarterbacks on Baltimore's roster while creating a clearer path for Brissett to take control of the offense.

The Ravens could still make additional moves to address their depth, particularly with Jackson unavailable for at least four games and Huntley's injury expected to keep him sidelined for an extended period.

What's next for Ravens quarterback depth chart?

Brissett is expected to start when Baltimore hosts the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday, Nov. 16, giving the veteran additional time to learn Doyle's offensive system.

Fagnano and Slovis remain options behind Brissett, though the coaching staff will need to decide how to structure the quarterback room moving forward. The Ravens have struggled to generate consistent offense over the past month, and their passing attack has become increasingly limited without Jackson. Brissett's arrival won't immediately solve the offensive line's protection issues or Baltimore's inability to sustain drives, but it gives Minter and Doyle an experienced quarterback who can stabilize the position.

With the Ravens sitting below .500 and facing growing pressure to turn their season around, the latest roster move represents another step in Baltimore's attempt to salvage its season.

articles.title: Cowboys’ Jerry Jones Makes Decisive Statement on NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is taking his team into the NFL trade deadline, and he has a clear vision of where things are heading. The post Cowboys’ Jer...
articles.body:
Selling? No, the Dallas Cowboys will not be selling at the NFL trade deadline, which looms in just four days. The team must play a game–a pretty important game, really, as all these games are now made much more important thanks to recent failures–against the Colts on the road and, in doing so, they will see what a team in the midst of a massive sell looks like. The Colts have dumped stars in the past 10 days, and could dump at least one more if running back Jonathan Taylor is sent out by Tuesday.

Might playing against a team in the throws of an on-the-fly rebuild inspire team owner Jerry Jones to shift his thinking and rebuild his spent draft capital? There has been ample conversation about trading away George Pickens, but that has apparently been more smoke than fire. But whether things could change was the question put to Jones on Friday afternoon during a radio appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, and the owner was clear in his stance.

Cowboys 'Commitment' Won't Change at NFL Trade Deadline

Jones still thinks the 2026 Cowboys can be a good team. It's an absurd thought based on the results so far, but maybe not so absurd when you consider the talent level on this team and the fact that the Cowboys are 3-5 and somehow still in a good position to win their otherwise terrible division.

"I have, I really believe that we have a team that the work we have done over the last 18 months, last year and this year, has real potential to play better than it's played now. My situation, and I am not talking about Indianapolis, I am not talking about any other team, our situation, because the amount and the commitment and the changes we have made, it's not the smart thing to do to make big adjustments. I would much more likely be adding to this direction than taking away from it."

The Cowboys will play the Colts on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET in Indianapolis. The NFL trade deadline follows on Tuesday, November 10.

articles.title: "Patrick tears up. All this stuff going on": How Patrick Mahomes turned an ordinary Mavericks visit into an emotional moment for a grieving Chiefs fan
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes had already become one of the NFL's biggest names by the summer of 2019.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes had already become one of the NFL's biggest names by the summer of 2019. But a visit to the Dallas Mavericks that year gave people a glimpse of something beyond his football skills. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback met a fan who had lost several close relatives within a year. What started as an ordinary interaction turned emotional when the man opened up about his struggles and explained how watching Mahomes and the Chiefs had helped him get through the difficult period.Mahomes was in Fort Worth, Texas, training with his longtime personal trainer Bobby Stroupe and his APEC group. During the visit, he got to meet NBA legend Dirk Nowitzki. However, another encounter ended up becoming one of the most memorable parts of the day. A Chiefs fan working at the Mavericks' pro shop was too shy to approach the quarterback. Mahomes noticed him and decided to make the first move.Patrick Mahomes gets emotional after Chiefs fan shares painful family lossThe fan wore Chiefs gear and started crying almost immediately when Mahomes approached him. He told the quarterback that he had lost several close relatives over the previous year. Following the losses, watching the Chiefs play had become a source of comfort and helped him keep his spirits up.Stroupe witnessed the exchange and later recalled how Mahomes reacted. In an August 19, 2019, interview with The Kansas City Star, he described the moment with a simple but powerful observation."Patrick, like, tears up," Stroupe said. "All this stuff going on, he locked in with this young man, giving him everything he had until the kid didn't know what to say any more."The trainer's account showed that Mahomes did not treat the meeting like another quick fan interaction. He stayed focused on the man and gave him his attention. There were no cameras or a planned public appearance driving the moment. Mahomes had simply noticed a fan who wanted to meet him and walked over.The encounter also stayed with the quarterback. When asked about it months later, Mahomes remembered the moment immediately. For Stroupe, that response said a lot about how naturally the Chiefs star understood other people's feelings. Bobby Stroupe reveals what made Patrick Mahomes' gesture specialStroupe had worked with Mahomes since fourth grade, long before the quarterback became an NFL MVP. He had seen his personality develop over the years and believed empathy was one of his strongest qualities.Speaking to The Kansas City Star on August 19, 2019, Stroupe explained why Mahomes understood the significance of the fan's experience."What that moment meant to (the fan), Patrick is intelligent enough to recognize that immediately," he said.He also described the way Mahomes thinks about the people around him."He's thoughtful about, 'What are other people experiencing in this moment that I'm here, and how can I affect that?'"That awareness, according to Stroupe, was not limited to interactions with fans. He also pointed to Mahomes remembering teammates' birthdays, looking out for children who were often picked last and treating people around him with consideration.Chiefs general manager Brett Veach shared a similar view in the same 2019 profile. He described Mahomes as someone who notices everything, including how much work goes into success and how people conduct themselves.The Mavericks visit was supposed to be an opportunity for Mahomes to meet Nowitzki, a basketball star he had admired growing up. Instead, the day also gave him an unexpected chance to connect with someone going through a painful time.For the grieving fan, that conversation offered a personal moment with the player whose team had helped him through a year of loss. And for those who knew Mahomes, it was another example of why his impact in Kansas City extended well beyond the football field.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 49ers rumors: Brandon Aiyuk’s reinstatement chances ‘not promising’ in 2026
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers boast one of the most recognizable NFL rosters from a names perspective and wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, who spoke to media on Friday...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers boast one of the most recognizable NFL rosters from a names perspective and wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, who spoke to media on Friday , November 6, is certainly one of them. articles.title: ESPN re-grades Jaguars, Raiders Jakobi Meyers trade one year later
articles.summary: ESPN re-graded the Jaguars and Raiders trade for WR Jakobi Meyers one year later.
articles.body:
With the 2026 NFL trade deadline near, ESPN's Seth Walder went back and re-graded each trade deadline deal from 2025, including the Jacksonville Jaguars' move for WR Jakobi Meyers.

To acquire Meyers, the Jaguars sent 2026 fourth- and sixth-round picks to the Las Vegas Raiders .

When the trade was first made, Walder gave the Jaguars a C+ for the deal. Now, he gives Jacksonville a B+.

"Meyers has been a helpful player in his own right, recording 1.6 yards per route run since arriving in Jacksonville," Walder wrote. "And Trevor Lawrence has also ranked seventh in QBR in the NFL in that span. That is no doubt a confluence of many factors, but having a reliable No. 2 receiver like Meyers is one of them."

Immediately upon his arrival to Jacksonville, Meyers made a big impact. His skill set makes him a terrific fit for the Coen offense. He can be moved around pre-snap, while in the passing game, Meyers is comfortable and effective attacking the middle and intermediate parts of the football field -- not to mention that he's a willing run blocker as well.

This role can help open up opportunities for others and also creates plenty of targets for Meyers, who has been a reliable pass-catcher throughout his career.

Meyers' play was quickly rewarded with an in-season contract extension.

This season has been much of the same. Meyers has caught 26 of 36 passes for 374 yards with two touchdowns. Of his 26 receptions, 22 have picked up a first down.

"In retrospect, the fourth- and sixth-round picks they surrendered for Meyers were worth it for the Jaguars considering the team's uptick in play," Walder wrote. "I had considered him a rental prior to the trade, but Meyers signed an extension before the end of the season that was worth $20 million per year. So he isn't a value going forward but is important to a 2026 Jaguars team that's among the best in the AFC."

Walder gave the Raiders an A- when the trade was first made. His new grade for Las Vegas is slightly lower at a B+.

articles.title: 49ers-Raiders: DeForest Buckner's impact? Cousins to Bowers a problem?
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers return to the field on Sunday after their bye week to host the Las Vegas Raiders. Our writers weigh in on key questions ahead of the...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers return to the field on Sunday after their bye week to host the Las Vegas Raiders. Kyle Shanahan 's 49ers (6-1) are looking to bounce back from a 29-20 letdown in Atlanta, their first loss of the season, and the trade deadline looms on Tuesday. We asked staff writers Eric Branch and Harrison Rich and columnist Ann Killion to weigh in on some key questions ahead of the matchup against the Raiders (4-4).

How much of an impact will the acquisition of defensive tackle DeForest Buckner have on the 49ers? Where would you rank this in the pantheon of their midseason trades in recent years?

Eric Branch: It obviously ranks below the 2022 Christian McCaffrey blockbuster on the deadline Richter scale and it's not quite on par with the 2019 Emmanuel Sanders deal. At 32, Buckner is still an impact player (surprise: GM John Lynch maintains he's playing the best of his 11-year career), but, unlike the 2019 49ers' room that Sanders massively upgraded, the 49ers' banged-up defensive interior has been stouter than expected, largely thanks to the quick emergence of fourth-round rookie steal Gracen Halton.

Ann Killion: We'll figure out where this trade ranks at the end of the season based on the results: If they get to a Super Bowl and win it and Buckner plays a role, it will be an all-timer. Even without knowing how the trade turns out, I like the move a lot. Buckner is still a really good player, he was miserable with the situation in Indianapolis, the Colts were having a fire-sale and he fits perfectly with the 49ers 2026 season theme of "getting the band back together." It was a no-brainer.

Harrison Rich: This is no midseason move for prime McCaffrey, but it's certainly more aggressive than last season's deadline move for Keion White. Buckner is no longer at his peak. This is not the same player 49ers fans have fond memories of watching back in 2019, but he is still a good player at age 32, and his sheer presence will make life easier for the rest of the Niners defense. He will draw double teams, and fellow defensive linemen will receive more one-on-one opportunities. Buckner moves the needle, for sure, but it's hard to say this is the trade that puts the 49ers over the top in the postseason.

The 49ers are still in the market for a wide receiver. How hard should they push to acquire a stopgap at the position, or should they seek a front-line wideout in case injuries to Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel turn out to be more severe than anticipated?

Branch: Evans is clearly their most impactful wideout. He's 33, has been sidelined by Achilles tendinits since Oct. 19 and Lynch said this week there is "hope" that he can return to play in the "coming weeks" while invoking McCaffrey's 2024 bout with the same injury that sidelined him for eight games. Still, the 6-1 start means the 49ers don't have to panic to trade for a fill-in. And their failed pursuit of Vikings WR Jauan Jennings , which would have been a relatively low-wattage trade, suggests they are looking for more stopgap than superstar.

They have to be in the market for a wide receiver, considering their dire situation. Evans is a superstar but he got hurt in mid-October and even if he returns, at 33 there's no guarantee he's going to stay healthy the rest of the way. The 49ers have a lot of receiver talent supposedly coming off injuries soon, but as we've learned too well with this team, injured players don't always bounce back the way the team hopes. There are some long, cold months ahead.

Seek a difference-making wideout. This is the 49ers' best remaining chance, with a 6-1 record and relatively good health, to win a Super Bowl with this core. Receiver is the team's biggest need. You should let Evans rest as long as he needs to, as long as he's healthy in January. You can't rely on Samuel or Demarcus Robinson or rookie De'Zhaun Stribling , all coming off injuries, to get back to their preseason levels at this point. Go get a running mate for Evans and another weapon for Purdy, who has clearly been struggling to connect with his receivers as of late.

The 49ers have had some struggles covering tight ends this year (Trey McBride, the Falcons group). Is there a concern that the Kirk Cousins to Brock Bowers combination could be a significant problem Sunday?

The 49ers did allow their first two TDs to tight ends in the Week 7 loss in Atlanta, and McBride had nine catches for 75 yards in Week 3. Still, the presence of linebackers Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw is a big reason why the 49ers have actually been largely effective against tight ends: They are allowing six catches and 43.6 yards per game to the position. Like McBride, Bowers is good enough to inflate those numbers. He missed the first two regular-season games with a knee injury, but his per-game averages this season would translate to 116 catches for 1,550 yards and 14 TDs over 17 games.

Killion: Sure it could be a problem. Cousins to Bowers will be defensive coordinator Raheem Morris' biggest concern. Bowers is the Raiders' biggest threat so he'll get a lot of attention and, like Harrison points out, the 49ers will be willing to see if someone else can beat them. It will be fun to see what Shanahan protege Klint Kubiak cooks up against his one-time mentor.

The Cousins-to-Bowers connection is difficult for any opposing defense to contain. Cousins owns some of the best numbers among quarterbacks in 2026, and as Eric notes, Bowers has been on a tear. Bowers had two touchdowns last week against the Jets, and he reached the end zone in three of his prior five matchups. The 49ers might be best off doubling Bowers - or at least giving him extra attention - and forcing someone else to beat them.

Injuries will force the 49ers to trot out an underwhelming WR group for the second straight game after this crew's lack of production factored into their first loss of the season. The good news for the 49ers: They might be able to overwhelm the porous Raiders defense with Purdy, McCaffrey and Kittle doing nearly all the lifting. 49ers 27, Raiders 16

The 49ers got their bad loss out of the way two weeks ago, losing to Atlanta before the bye week, giving them a bad taste over their break. Now, they're rested and relaxed and ready for the final 10 games of the season. Shanahan is 6-1 after the bye week in the last seven years. 49ers 35, Raiders 20

A struggling 49ers offense against a struggling Raiders defense should make for an interesting matchup. Las Vegas has allowed at least 30 points in five straight weeks. The Rams put up 35 on them, and the Patriots scored 45. But this is a sneaky good offense led by Cousins. So if the Niners can't reach that 30-point mark at minimum, things could get dicey. 49ers 33, Raiders 24

articles.title: “But it's outrageous”: Deion Sanders’ son Shilo Sanders blasts New York’s $12,000 rent prices as $11.89 million bankruptcy case continues
articles.summary: Shilo Sanders has another problem on his hands, and this time it has nothing to do with football.
articles.body: Shilo Sanders has another problem on his hands, and this time it has nothing to do with football. The former Colorado Buffaloes safety is looking for a new home, but New York's rental market has left him questioning whether the move is worth it. Even with a budget that could stretch to $12,000 a month, Deion Sanders' son is struggling to find an apartment that offers enough space for the money.The search comes during a difficult financial period for Shilo, who remains involved in an $11.89 million bankruptcy dispute. He has already walked away from several expensive rentals in Florida. Now, New York has given him another reason to think twice about where he wants to settle. Deion Sanders' son Shilo Sanders questions New York apartments charging $12,000 a monthShilo did not hold back when he discussed New York's housing market in a YouTube video shared on November 6, 2026. He spoke about rental prices while getting his haircut, pointing out that the biggest problem was not necessarily the monthly cost but the limited space tenants received in return.“My biggest thing about New York, bro, is the square footage for the price,” Shilo said.He went on to explain that even apartments costing as much as $12,000 a month did not seem worth the asking price.“I don't know who normalized the real estate market in New York, but it's outrageous, bro,” he added.His reaction followed several weeks of house hunting in Florida. One property in Downtown Miami particularly caught his attention because of its river views. However, the rental prices proved too high, with some options costing more than $10,000 a month.West Palm Beach was another possibility, but safety concerns made him hesitant about returning there. New York initially looked like a fresh option. However, its rental market has not made the decision any easier.Shilo had even asked his YouTube audience whether he should move to the city. He had suggested that since he already lived in Florida, things could not get much worse. His latest comments suggest he may have underestimated New York's housing costs. Shedeur Sanders offers financial help as Shilo's $11.89 million bankruptcy case continuesThere is also a family offer that could help Shilo with his next move. In October 2026, his brother Shedeur Sanders, the Cleveland Browns quarterback, offered to cover the down payment on a house Shilo chooses. However, Shilo would remain responsible for the monthly rent.That arrangement comes as his bankruptcy case remains unresolved. The dispute goes back to a 2015 altercation involving Shilo and John Darjean, a security guard at his high school. Darjean later secured an $11.89 million judgment against him.Shilo filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in 2023 and has maintained that he acted in self-defense during the incident. The five-day bankruptcy trial brought the dispute back into focus, but Judge Michael Romero has yet to deliver a final decision.The judge also raised concerns about missing surveillance footage that could help clarify what happened. The absence of those videos has left an important part of the case unresolved.Shilo did receive some relief in another legal dispute. Barnes & Thornburg LLP had filed a lawsuit over approximately $170,000 in unpaid legal bills. However, the case was dismissed with prejudice in October 2026.Away from football, Shilo has been exploring fashion, modelling, acting, music and content creation. New York could offer opportunities in several of those fields, but the rental prices have clearly become a major hurdle.Currently, Shedeur's offer gives him some financial support with his housing plans. Finding a place he actually likes, without committing to another expensive monthly bill, remains the bigger challenge.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Rams safety Quentin Lake apologizes to Justin Herbert for 'deli meat' comment, even though he has a point
articles.summary: Quentin Lake said Justin Herbert was "throwing deli meat" and "seeing ghosts" on the "St. Brown Podcast" after his interception against the Chargers.
articles.body: One of the weird things about modern sports is that current athletes will gladly hop on podcasts. Of course, that sometimes makes things awkward, as was the case for Rams safety Quentin Lake. Lake went on the "St. Brown Podcast" hosted by Lions receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and his brother Equanimeous St. Brown. On the show, Lake talked about an interception he made on Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers and was not complimentary of quarterback Justin Herbert's play. JUSTIN HERBERT, MADISON BEER GRILLED BY NFL LEGEND MICHAEL IRVIN AFTER EMBARRASSING CHARGERS LOSS "He was throwing deli meat out there," Lake said on the St. Brown Podcast. "He's seeing ghosts. I don't know what's going on, but we knew we were gonna get a couple. At least one." Alright, just a couple of guys being dudes, talking smack. Also, have you seen the 0-7 Chargers this year? "Throwing deli meat" might be a compliment compared to what they've done at times during the season. Seeing ghosts would actually be a welcome explanation. So, no harm, no foul. Nothing wrong with a little smack talk in the NFL. Oh, wait. He apologized? CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE According to The Los Angeles Times, Lake sent an apology to Herbert over text message, but had not heard back. "I don’t know if he read it," Lake said. "He probably says, 'I don’t care about it anymore. I’m not trying to see this. It doesn’t matter. You said what you said.' But at the same time I … felt like it was right for me to at least say, 'Hey, man, I didn’t mean it in any disrespectful way.'" Come on, Justin: He meant you were throwing deli meat in the most respectful way imaginable! CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Good on Lake for apologizing. But let's be honest, there's nothing wrong with a little off-field smack talk. And if Herbert is offended by his passes being compared to someone flinging some Boar's Head around, then maybe work on not leading the league with ten interceptions. That should be the rule: as long as you're at the top of the picks-thrown leaderboard, everyone gets to say you're throwing deli meat.

articles.title: Packers Get Discouraging Trade Message On Colts’ Jonathan Taylor
articles.summary: The Packers have shown interest in Colts RB Jonathan Taylor, but a new assessment raises several questions about whether Green Bay can make a deal work. The...
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers have been among the teams interested in Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, but a new assessment suggests a blockbuster deal is unlikely, even with the NFL trade deadline approaching.

Green Bay's rushing offense has struggled through eight games, yet one Packers beat writer believes the reasons go beyond who is carrying the football. And the Packers' draft-pick situation presents another obstacle.

Packers Get Discouraging Jonathan Taylor Trade Assessment

The Athletic's Matt Schneidman cast doubt on Green Bay acquiring Taylor or two other running backs mentioned as trade candidates.

"I don't see the Packers trading for a Jonathan Taylor, Breece Hall or Tony Pollard," Schneidman wrote.

The biggest issue isn't necessarily Taylor's talent. Schneidman argued that "the run game's biggest problem is the blocking," making an expensive backfield addition a questionable fix.

Taylor, a former Wisconsin star and three-time Pro Bowler, might also cost a first-round pick. Green Bay already sent its 2027 first-round selection to Dallas as part of the Micah Parsons trade last year.

Even if the Colts lower their demands, Schneidman questioned whether the Packers would part with two middle-round selections. He also didn't see an obvious Green Bay player who would entice another team in a trade package.

Then there's Josh Jacobs. The veteran returned in October after spending six games on the commissioner's exempt list and remains under an NFL investigation involving additional allegations. Jacobs said Wednesday that he isn't concerned about missing more games.

Schneidman acknowledged a longer absence for Jacobs could change the Packers' thinking. Otherwise, acquiring Taylor would create another question: Would Green Bay keep both backs, or try to move Jacobs?

He also expressed doubts about the logic of pursuing Pollard, who is at a similar career stage to Jacobs. Taylor and Hall could represent longer-term options, but fitting either alongside Jacobs would be difficult.

Packers Have Reportedly Checked In on Colts' Jonathan Taylor

The assessment contrasts with reports that Green Bay is interested in acquiring Taylor. NFL.com's Bobby Kownack reported that the Packers were among teams showing interest, citing NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz also previously named Green Bay among interested teams, along with Minnesota, Denver, Cincinnati and the New York Giants . He said the asking price was considered too high, although a trade remained possible.

Indianapolis has already traded Quenton Nelson to Seattle and DeForest Buckner to San Francisco. Schultz reported Thursday that the Colts plan to revisit offers after Sunday's game against Dallas unless a team makes an exceptional proposal beforehand.

For Green Bay, the need is apparent. The Packers entered Week 10 averaging an NFL-low 60.6 rushing yards per game. Jacobs has managed 75 yards on 32 carries since returning to the lineup.

Coach Matt LaFleur has suggested the responsibility goes beyond the backfield. Following Green Bay's win over Carolina, he said inconsistent blocking details, execution and play calls have all contributed to the struggles.

"I would say it was more the collective," LaFleur said.

The Packers also have other positions to consider before Tuesday's deadline, including offensive line, defensive tackle and tight end. Spending significant draft capital on Taylor would leave fewer resources to address those needs.

Taylor would provide immediate star power, but his arrival wouldn't automatically improve the blocking in front of him. That's the argument Schneidman raises as general manager Brian Gutekunst weighs whether to pursue a blockbuster or focus on smaller improvements.

The Carolina Panthers are considering potential adjustments to their offensive line ahead of Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the Denver Broncos . After struggling to keep quarterback Bryce Young protected in recent weeks, the coaching staff is assessing different options in an effort to put together a more dependable unit.

"Bryce Young has had 11 sacks in the last two weeks," Fowler said. "He was under constant duress in that Thursday night game against Green Bay. So he was asked about it today. He would not tip his hand on that, but I know they have at least evaluated that situation.

articles.title: Steelers-Chargers Trade Idea Swaps Former 3rd-Round Pick for 1,000-Yard WR
articles.summary: The Steelers could address their receiving problems with a proposed Chargers deal that would reunite Roman Wilson with his former college coach. The post Ste...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers could get Aaron Rodgers another proven receiver before the NFL trade deadline, but one proposed deal would come at the expense of a young wideout and a valuable draft pick.

The proposed trade would send Roman Wilson to the Los Angeles Chargers, where he would reunite with former Michigan coach Jim Harbaugh. In return, Pittsburgh would land a receiver who surpassed 1,000 yards as a rookie and could become a long-term piece of its offense.

Steelers-Chargers Trade Proposal Sends Roman Wilson for Ladd McConkey

In a look at four potential Steelers trades, CBS Sports' Bryan DeArdo proposed Pittsburgh acquiring Ladd McConkey and a 2027 fifth-round pick from the Chargers in exchange for Wilson and a 2027 second-round selection.

The deal would give Pittsburgh an established receiver while sending Wilson back to the coach he played under during Michigan's national championship season.

"It's possible that the Steelers wouldn't have to part with Wilson in this scenario," DeArdo wrote.

However, he suggested the Chargers would likely want another receiver if they were willing to surrender McConkey, making Wilson an intriguing option because of his history with Harbaugh.

Wilson caught 48 passes for 789 yards and 12 touchdowns during his final season at Michigan in 2023. He was a key part of the Wolverines' undefeated championship run before Pittsburgh selected him in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft.

His NFL career hasn't followed the same trajectory. Injuries have limited his opportunities, although Wilson has recorded 14 receptions for 188 yards and two touchdowns in five appearances this season.

McConkey would bring considerably more notable production.

The former Georgia standout caught 82 passes for 1,149 yards and seven touchdowns during his rookie season in 2024. He followed that with 66 receptions for 789 yards and six scores in 2025.

Through six games this season, McConkey has 17 receptions for 286 yards and one touchdown.

Still, getting the Chargers to surrender one of their most productive young receivers would present a considerable challenge.

"The Chargers also probably don't want to part with McConkey," DeArdo said.

The proposed second-round pick could make the conversation more interesting, particularly with Wilson giving Harbaugh a familiar receiver to develop.

Steelers Would Sacrifice Valuable Draft Pick for Ladd McConkey

Pittsburgh's need for another receiving threat has become difficult to ignore despite its 6-2 record and first-place standing in the AFC North.

DK Metcalf leads Steelers receivers with 33 catches for 378 yards and one touchdown. Rookie Germie Bernard has contributed 32 receptions for 284 yards, while tight ends Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington have helped Rodgers move the offense.

However, Wilson's injury issues and Michael Pittman Jr.'s absence have limited Pittsburgh's options.

McConkey could provide a more established target alongside Metcalf, potentially giving Rodgers another reliable option during what the quarterback has said will be his final NFL season.

That retirement plan also makes the proposed compensation difficult for general manager Omar Khan.

Pittsburgh will need to continue its search for a long-term quarterback in 2027, and surrendering a second-round selection would remove a valuable asset from that process.

DeArdo acknowledged that concern, explaining that receiving a fifth-round pick would at least partially offset the loss of the earlier selection.

McConkey's rookie contract is another selling point. He remains under contract through the 2027 season, meaning Pittsburgh would be acquiring more than a short-term option for Rodgers.

Of course, the proposal is only a hypothetical deal, with no indication the Chargers are shopping McConkey or discussing a trade with Pittsburgh.

The Harbaugh-Wilson connection gives the idea an interesting wrinkle. But the Steelers would still have to convince Los Angeles that a reunion with its coach and a second-round pick are worth parting with a proven young receiver.
